title: SuperFrustum rewrite rules (hill-crossing primitive pairs)
what_a_rule_is: Two SuperFrustum parameter settings A and B that give (nearly) the same shape, separated by a hill: the straight path between them passes through clearly different shapes, so gradient descent started at A does not reach B. A rule maps A to B in one step.

tiers.exact: holds for every primitive; the jump is free
tiers.conditional: holds when applies_when is true; check it first
tiers.canonicalize: A and B are the same shape with no hill between them (a flat valley); pick one canonical form rather than jumping
tiers.approximate: B is only close to A (and the map is fitted, not derived); apply, then refine a few steps. Low confidence

thresholds.shape_distance: mean |sdf_A - sdf_B| over near-surface + uniform samples, divided by the primitive scale
thresholds.barrier: max shape distance along the straight A->B path above the endpoints

selection.note: rules below these supports are in the run's rules.json

parameter_layout.name: roundness
parameter_layout.meaning: corner radius of the base cross-section, relative to min(sx, sy)/2

parameter_layout.name: dilate
parameter_layout.meaning: uniform 3D dilation (rounded offset of the whole solid)

parameter_layout.name: taper
parameter_layout.meaning: top/base scale along z; 1 = no taper

parameter_layout.name: bulge
parameter_layout.meaning: bend of the z axis into an arc; sign = bend direction, 0 is singular (use +-1e-3 as neutral)

feature_definitions.round_minus_inset: roundness - (1 - taper); >= 0 is when a taper flip is exact

how_to_apply: theta is the 14-vector in parameter space (parameter_layout). For exact/conditional/canonicalize rules the transform block is complete: optional taper flip, then local rotation (rotate the shape frame by local_rotation_matrix, compose into the world rotation, re-order sizes by size_permutation), then optional bulge negation. Reference code: op_taper_flip / op_group / op_bulge_flip in experiments/rewrite_pairs/transforms.py; transforms.apply_rule takes legacy_rule_id with the run's rules.json. Check applies_when with feature_definitions first.
